surfaces.part: white dome cap on sign box
sign box (teal header with ring, tan number panel)

answer.evidence: The width profile is 6, 8, 8 at rows 0-2, then 10 from row 3 to row 19. The white cap is a hat rounded only at its top edge, with a flat bottom sitting on a wider sign box. It does not widen and then narrow again, and it does not overhang the shaft. Row 3 is a thin teal line and row 4 is a dark outline, so there is no separate top plane with an eave shadow. The sign box is drawn only as a vertical face: a teal header with a ring, then a tan panel with the number 3. The pole (rows 20-26, width 6) and the base (rows 27-31, width 12) are also drawn only as front faces, with at most a 1-row top edge on the base. This matches the red 'flat band cap' and 'front elevation' references, not the green ellipse-cap column.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a thin sign post (a pole with a small lantern-like sign head and a numeral 3), so sparseness alone is not held against it. Measured facts: 9 visible tones per tile, above bus-shelter-a (6) and below kiosk-a (12) and vending-a (20). Near-flat coverage is 0%, and dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline is tinted and reads as a dark blue-grey material tone rather than a black sticker line. By eye, the sign head has a light/mid/dark split plus a highlight, but the pole is only 2-3 steps with little grain or detail. Next to the richer vending and kiosk references it looks slightly thinner and flatter, with fewer shading steps (about 4 against 5-6) and no per-surface texture dots. It is acceptable against bus-shelter-a but not equal to the better references, and in doubt this fails.

surfaces.part: white hat on top of the sign box
teal header band with ring symbol
tan number panel (main sign box face)

answer.evidence: The top end is a small white hat. The width profile goes 6, 8, 8 and then jumps to 10 at row 3, so it is rounded only at its upper edge and sits flat on the wider sign box. That makes it a hat, not an ellipse plate that widens and narrows again. The box below it (rows 3-19, width 10) is drawn only as vertical faces: a teal header, then a tan number panel. Row 3 is a lighter teal line, but a dark outline row follows directly at row 4. No top plane with a front-edge line and eave shadow is visible, so the top is at most 2 rows. The pole (rows 20-26, width 6) and the base (rows 27-31, width 12) read as a plain flat elevation, so the whole object is a front view.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a thin pole-style sign with a small lamp-like head and a numbered panel. It measures 9 visible tones per full tile, above bus-shelter-a (6) and below kiosk-a (12) and vending-a (20). Near-flat coverage is 0%, and the dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline is tinted and not near-black. The picture agrees: the outline is a dark blue-grey that leans toward the neighbouring material. The pole and head show roughly 3-4 steps with a highlight edge, which is a bit shallower than the vending machine's multi-step ramps. The piece is thin and sparse, so the density fact is not held against it. By eye it is a little simpler and slimmer than the kiosk and vending references, but it is clean, has no flat fills, and is comparable to the bus shelter. It is close to the lower end of the shipped standard without looking like a sticker, but it is not clearly equal to the stronger references, and when in doubt the rule is to fail.
